observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A wide, low rosette made of many broad, ruffled, wavy-edged lobes in rust-red to maroon with orange-tan rims. The lobes overlap in two or three tiers and cup slightly upward. The centre is dark and glossy and looks wet, with shiny highlights pooling between the inner lobes. It sits on a transparent background with no ground or shadow. The surface is smooth and glossy, closer to a soft 3D render than to painted strokes, and there is no outline. It is wider than it is tall and low-domed rather than completely flat. There is no green anywhere. Taken as a whole, it looks a lot like a cluster of ruffled cup or jelly fungus (wood-ear / Peziza-like) or a red lettuce/rose-like rosette.

At max zoom the mat lies in one cell beside the vanilla human. It fills most of the cell's width, sits in the lower half and comes to well below the human's waist, so it reads as low ground cover. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a small red-brown ruffled blob, still readable as a reddish low growth on the ground.

SIGNATURE.seen: It is a spreading rosette of fleshy rust-maroon lobes with a glossy wet centre and no green, which is what the description names.

READS_KIND.seen: It is low and spreading and reads as a ground-cover rosette, not a hill. It is low-domed and ruffled rather than truly crust-flat, which I note as polish.

NATURAL.seen: The lobes are organic and irregular; nothing looks constructed.

ANCHOR.seen: It rests on the bottom portion of the canvas, centred, with nothing cut off.

NO_SCENERY.seen: Real alpha, with no clay patch, shadow or ground disc. The wet sheen is on the plant itself.

ALIEN.seen: The ruffled, glossy, red-brown cupped lobes with a wet centre read at a glance as a cluster of jelly or cup fungus (wood-ear-like), or a red ruffled lettuce/rose rosette. The card explicitly forbids fungus, flower and succulent readings.

STYLE.seen: It is realistic, not cute or cartoonish, although the smooth glossy shading leans toward a 3D-render look rather than painterly vanilla and has no outline.

OURS.seen: It is a bespoke picture that matches the description; it is not vanilla or donor art.

FILLS.seen: It spans nearly the full canvas width, and its visible height is 148 px. That is sensible for a mat.

SCALE.seen: Beside the human it is knee-to-shin high and about a cell wide, which fits a ground mat.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a distinct red-brown ruffled patch.

VARIANTS.seen: Only one picture was supplied and there is no variants panel.

edits.change: The mat is a flat crust of thick, tightly packed rust-maroon scale-plates with angular, cracked-clay-like margins, interlocking in an irregular tessellated pattern that radiates outward from a glistening wet seam at the centre.

The plates lie pressed flush against the clay ground, the whole growth a thin crust spread in a wide low ellipse, seen from above at a slight angle, with a flat profile and every plate edge resting on the ground.
Painterly brush texture across the plates in vanilla RimWorld style, with a thin clean dark outline around the outer edge of the mat, readable at normal zoom.

Shallow fleshy plates with a slightly recessed wet centre; the mature growth lies close against the ground as a spreading crust, plates shading from dry dusty rust at the rim to dark wet maroon at the centre.

Wet highlights are small and restrained, concentrated only around the central seam; the plate surfaces carry matte, textured painterly shading with visible brush marks, and the outer contour is a clean dark line.

invariants: rust-maroon / red-brown palette with no green anywhere on the plant
single plant centred on a transparent background
ground-hugging spreading mat that fills about 95% of the tile
reads as an unnamed alien ground-cover, not a known Earth organism
request.prompt: A single flat ground-cover mat for a RimWorld plant sprite, drawn in painterly vanilla RimWorld style with visible brush texture, realistic, on a transparent background. The qirra mat is a thin crust spread in a wide low ellipse, viewed from above at a slight angle, lying flush against cracked canyon clay. Its body is made of thick, tightly packed rust-maroon scale-plates with angular margins like cracked clay, interlocking in an irregular tessellated pattern and radiating outward from a glistening wet seam at the centre. The plates are shallow and fleshy, lying pressed against the ground with every edge resting on the clay; the profile is flat and the whole growth reads as a crust. Colour runs from dry, dusty rust-brown at the rim to dark wet maroon at the recessed centre; the palette is entirely red-brown and rust-maroon. Plate surfaces are matte with textured painterly shading and visible brush marks; small restrained wet highlights sit only around the central seam. A thin, clean dark outline traces the outer edge of the mat and stays readable at normal zoom. The mat fills the tile and is centred, with no ground, no background and no other objects. It is an alien ground-cover with its own invented form. Reference: none; build the body from this description.
